mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, which reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or the effect size is smaller than the 95% confidence interval of the estimated coefficient.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months signals disinflation, prompting a reduction in rate hike expectations and a subsequent rally in equities, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 100 similar episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically different from the prior month's return (p > 0.05), or the effect size is smaller than the 90% confidence interval.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in the next month
failure_condition: In analogous labor market tightening episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than zero (p > 0.10), or the interaction term is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% signals weakening manufacturing momentum, which elevates recession risk and reduces equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 10 prior similar INDPRO declines, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.15), or the effect size is within one standard error of zero.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds its prior month's level by more than 5% in a month where GDP growth is flat, it indicates resilient consumer demand, prompting optimism about corporate earnings and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% and GDP growth is flat in the current month
regime_hint: Resilient demand shock in flat GDP environment
failure_condition: Across 20 analogous demand shocks, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or the interaction coefficient is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period where FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months, the persistence of high policy rates erodes risk appetite and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 15 prior high-rate regimes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or the effect size is within one standard error of zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% accompanied by a sustained rise in PAYEMS (over 8 months) indicates a labor market transition toward full employment, which supports optimism for corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while PAYEMS increases for ≥8 consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market transition to full employment
failure_condition: In 12 prior labor market transition episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than zero (p > 0.10), or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in RSAFS (retail sales) of more than 8% in two consecutive months, despite stable macro conditions, signals deteriorating consumer confidence and supply chain disruptions, which depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >8% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 prior RSAFS contractions, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.15), or the effect size is within one standard error of zero.
